subject: Silverpine private deployment — connectivity & implementation handoff
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Silverpine private deployment — connectivity & implementation handoff

Hi Samantha / Silverpine team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for your private deployment. Per our kickoff, this thread will be the working channel for the networking and implementation checklist so we have a single source of truth. High-level asks from our side to prepare for the implementation runbook:

- Confirm the preferred connectivity model: VPC peering, Vendor-hosted private endpoints (PrivateLink-style), or direct on-prem interconnect. If you already have a preference, note it.
- Share the networking contact who will approve firewall changes and coordinate the test window.
- Provide your planned CIDR ranges for Silverpine VPCs and any NAT/egress IPs (we need these for allowlist).
- Any compliance constraints (eg blocked external DNS, outbound egress limits) that might affect the on-prem package.

Proposed timeline: preflight & diagram review this week, connectivity dry-run (connectivity test) next Wednesday 2027-05-11, full runbook dry-run the following week. If that works I’ll assign Aditya to run the connectivity tests and Monica will lead the overall cutover coordination.

I’ve attached a short Redwood requirements doc to show what we expect from networking. If you can attach a simple network sketch (CIDRs, subnets, NAT, gateways) we’ll validate it and flag any blockers.

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin

Thanks Sam — 10:00 PT tomorrow works for us. Agenda for the 30-min sync:

1) Confirm connectivity model (peer vs private endpoint) and implications for routing.
2) Validate CIDR ranges + NAT/egress IP list for allowlisting.
3) Run through Redwood on‑prem package requirements (ports, certificates, DNS expectations).
4) Confirm dry-run window and assign owners.

Quick notes for the meeting:
- If you choose VPC peering, we’ll need: peerable CIDRs (no overlap), route table update plan, and a narrow allowlist of our egress IPs for outbound service calls.
- If you choose private endpoints, we’ll provide endpoint configuration guidance but we’ll need a path for mutual TLS and access to your private DNS.

I’ve re-attached the Redwood requirements doc for the call. Aditya will bring the connectivity test checklist.

—Marcus

Date: 2027-05-04T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Silverpine private deployment — connectivity & implementation handoff

Appreciate the clear agenda. Quick answers from network:

- Preferred model: VPC peering into our transit VPC (we can do PrivateLink but it adds an extra DNS/bolting step).
- CIDR ranges (planned): 10.10.0.0/16 (app VPC), 10.20.0.0/16 (transit VPC), 172.16.32.0/24 (on-prem AWS DirectConnect), egress NAT IPs: 54.33.12.45, 54.33.12.46.
- Firewall: we allow outbound to specific egress IPs only; any additional outbound endpoints must be allowlisted in advance.
- Compliance note: our SOC2 team requires a short evidence pack for host/network hardening and a list of logs you’ll write to the customer KMS/HSM. We can share the SOC checklist after the call.

Timeline: the 2027-05-11 connectivity test window looks good. We’ll reserve 09:00–11:00 PT for the test.

Questions for Redwood: what outbound ports should our NAT allow? Do you need any inbound ports for the on‑prem package? Also, can you confirm whether the Redwood appliance will require a public IP at any point during bootstrapping?

Thanks —
Jacob Lee
Network Engineering Lead (contractor for Silverpine)
jacob.lee@itfirm.io

> From: silverpine_vpc_network_sketch.pdf
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@itfirm.io>, Samantha Torres <s.torres@silverpine.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Silverpine private deployment — connectivity & implementation handoff

Thanks Jacob — quick answers inline and operational next steps.

- Outbound ports: Redwood needs HTTPS (443) outbound for model updates and telemetry; we also need TCP high ports for artifact transfer during install (we can provide an explicit port list — default 1024–65535, but we will scope to 50000–50050 for the appliance transfer if you prefer).
- Inbound ports: No inbound public ports required once peered. During bootstrap, the installer will initiate outbound connections only; we do not require a public inbound IP for normal operation. If you prefer a temporary public egress for initial image pull we can do that during a scheduled maintenance window.
- Bootstrapping: we support a NAT-only bootstrap (no public inbound) and will attempt to use your DirectConnect path for faster image pulls if the routes are in place.

Operational plan:
1) Marcus/Aditya to run a preflight checklist with Jacob on 2027-05-11 09:00 PT (connectivity test).
2) If green, schedule appliance installation dry-run 2027-05-18.
3) Final cutover targeted 2027-05-25 (tentative).

Action items assigned:
- Jacob: confirm route table updates and add redwood egress IPs to allowlist by 2027-05-09.
- Aditya: share connectivity-test-checklist.xlsx and runbook link (will attach).
- Marcus: validate SOC evidence needs with Security and share required fields.

I’ve attached the initial connectivity checklist for Aditya to use. Marcus — I’ll hand off coordination to you after the preflight so we have a single owner for the go/no-go decision.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

- Redwood will use egress NAT IPs 54.33.12.45/46 for allowlisting.
- No inbound public IP required for the appliance; we will bootstrap over outbound HTTPS and the DirectConnect path.

- Aditya: run connectivity test (2027-05-11 09:00–11:00 PT) using connectivity-test-checklist.xlsx.

- Monica: schedule appliance dry-run (2027-05-18) and runbook review.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the dry-run.

—Marcus
